newsitem.title: SPAIN: Barcelona's long-term mayor quits, surprises Spain.
newsitem.headline: Barcelona's long-term mayor quits, surprises Spain.

text.p: Barcelona's long-serving Socialist mayor Pasqual Maragall, who transformed Spain's second city into a thriving, dynamic port and successful 1992 Olympic Games host, has suddenly announced his resignation.

The move, made late on Saturday at a party conference, caught even his closest advisers by surprise. There was a stunned silence in the hall as the well-liked, personable Maragall, 54, said he wanted out after nearly 15 years as mayor.

He said there were three reasons behind his decision: a personal desire to leave politics, the decision of his major rival for the office, Catalan nationalist politician Miquel Roca, not to run again and his discontent with Barcelona's Socialist Party leaders.
"Now is the time to make decisions," he said. "I'm convinced that Barcelona has not tired of us, but I'm not so sure that the party of Barcelona has not tired of me."
Maragall said he would step down as mayor in September 1997 and would continue to serve as president of the European Union's Committee of the Regions until the end of next year.
He is widely credited with restoring Barcelona's lustre as an important Mediterranean port and with organising a smooth, successful Olympic Games.
"He is a great mayor of the city," Joan Puigdollers, city spokesman for rival Catalan Convergence and Unity alliance, said. "This closes an historic era in Barcelona's town hall."

Maragall had been seen as a likely successor to former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez as head of the Spain's Socialist Workers' Party because he was never tainted by the corruption scandals that eventually ended nearly 14 years of Socialist rule in May.
He did not indicate if he had completely ruled out a bid for the country's top political post.
Maragall named deputy mayor Joan Clos as his successor.
